newsitem.title: USA: Fergie says kids come first in talk show decision.
newsitem.headline: Fergie says kids come first in talk show decision.

text.p: Duchess of York Sarah Ferguson spoke publicly Tuesday about the possibility of hosting an American television talk show but said her children would come first.
"There's a lot of talk about it, but my babies are the most important thing in my life," Ferguson said during an appearance on NBC's late night talk show, The Tonight Show with Jay Leno.
"If anything did happen, it would have to be very much with them (children) coming first and they're in school in England," Ferguson said, referring to her daughters who are eight and six.
Ferguson, who is known by the nickname "Fergie", is meeting with network and studio executives this week to discuss the possibility of hosting a talk show.

British newspapers have reported Ferguson, who is currently promoting her book, My Story, has negotiated a $4.8 million Hollywood deal which could rise as high as $20 million if she meets television rating targets.
But Ferguson's spokesman, Jeff Schneider with public relations firm Howard Rubenstein in New York, said such reports have been premature.

"The executives are generally interested in having her do her own show after her success on several shows last month," said Schneider, referring to her appearances on Larry King Live, Oprah Winfrey and PrimeTime Live with Diane Sawyer in November.
"The idea is kind of different. I would really have to sit down and get a few tips from you (Leno) because you really need a very big background to do this (talk show)," Ferguson said Tuesday.
Ferguson divorced Britain's Prince Andrew this year.
